title: Exhaustion collapse asks only guard activeCount - encounter foes ignored, sight law bypassed
claim: DFU decides rest-vs-death on GameManager.AreEnemiesNearby() (PlayerEntity.cs:2397) - hostile enemies that see the player or would spawn in classic - and SetHealth(0) when true (PlayerEntity.cs:2440-2441). world.js:623 passes enemiesNearby: (cityGuards?.activeCount?.() ?? 0) > 0 into exhaustionOutcome - the exteriorFoes pool is not consulted at all (the same file's rest deps consult both pools, world.js:975-976), and activeCount has no sight/distance test. exterior.js:401 has the same coarse guard-only read. systems/rest.js:83-93 confirms enemiesNearby:true is the death arm.
consequence: Collapsing beside a detected encounter wolf yields the safe one-hour sleep instead of DFU's death; collapsing in town while one unaware guard is active anywhere kills the player where DFU grants the hour of rest.

verify.reason: world.js:623 and exterior.js:401 pass `enemiesNearby: (cityGuards?.activeCount?.() ?? 0) > 0` into exhaustionOutcome - only guards, exteriorFoes never consulted. DFU's CollapseFromExhaustion (PlayerEntity.cs:2397,2426,2440-2441) uses AreEnemiesNearby() (no resting narrowing), scanning ALL active enemy behaviours incl. encounter foes, then SetHealth(0). exteriorFoes exists in the same file (used correctly at 975-976) but is skipped here.

title: Travel map hasShip hardwired false - ship ownership and knight free-ship perk unwired
claim: DFU computes hasShip = DaggerfallBankManager.OwnsShip || GuildManager.FreeShipTravel() (TravelPopUp.cs:219). The port ships both halves - banking.ownsShip is live in worldModes.js:1231 and KnightlyOrder rank-6 freeShipTravel is ported (guildServices.js:336, zero callers) - but buildTravelMapWindow passes the literal `hasShip: false` (world.js:1728, with a stale 'a SHIP still has no ownership state' comment) and neither call site (world.js:1692/:1702) overrides it, so calculateTripCost's !hasShip arm (travel.js:86) always charges.
consequence: A player who bought a ship, or reached rank 6 in a knightly order, still pays 25 gold per 24 ocean pixels on every fast travel crossing water.

verify.reason: TravelPopUp.cs:219: hasShip = OwnsShip || FreeShipTravel(). banking.js:266 ownsShip() is live at worldModes.js:1231/3209, but guildServices.js:336 freeShipTravel() has zero callers anywhere. world.js:1728 passes hasShip:false literally into buildTravelMapWindow with a stale comment ('A SHIP still has no ownership state'); neither call site overrides it. travel.js:86: `if(oceanPixels>0 && !hasShip && travelShip) totalCost+=25*...` always charges. test/travel.test.js:63 only unit-tests calculateTripCost with hasShip passed explicitly - no wiring pin.

title: Static-NPC greetings expand no macros - npcSession's expandRandomTextRecord is a plain line join
claim: world.js wires NPCSession's expandRandomTextRecord as townTalk.lines(id).map(r=>r.text??r).join(' ') - no macro pass - while the AnswerPipeline below gets the real expandTalkRecord (world.js:2557). npcSession.talkToNpc (npcSession.js:529) draws the greeting (7206-7209 ladder or 8550-8571 guild table) through this seam. C# TalkToNpc (TalkManager.cs:2649) expands the greeting via ExpandRandomTextRecord, the full MacroHelper; the port's own greeting-set doc (talkSession.js:12-19) records these records carrying %pcf/%pcn/%cn/%oth.
consequence: Any static-NPC greeting variant carrying a macro shows the raw %-code on screen in every interior conversation opened through worldModes' static-NPC click; line joins also insert spaces where C# uses none.

verify.reason: C#'s single TalkToNpc (TalkManager.cs:2616-2663), used for both mobile and static NPCs, expands the greeting via ExpandRandomTextRecord (line 2649, full macros). worldModes.js:978 routes static-NPC clicks to npcSession.talkToStaticNPC -> talkToNpc (npcSession.js:463-529), whose greeting line uses deps.expandRandomTextRecord. That npcSession instance (world.js:2469) wires expandRandomTextRecord to a bare line-join (world.js:2488), distinct from the real macro-aware expander wired only into the separately-constructed AnswerPipeline (world.js:2557).

title: buildingCompassDirection seam never wired - every engine %di answers '...never mind...'
